# OpenCode conversation archiver

An OpenCode server plugin that archives every top-level conversation after each
completed turn. One package supports both OpenCode/GenCode majors: 1.x
(`>=1.17.18`) and 2.x (OpenCode V2, GenCode `2.2.0-gencode.*`), writing the same
archive format to the same repository on both. It keeps one Markdown file per session in a git repository and
records only user-visible text:

- user text parts;
- assistant text parts;
- context-compaction boundaries.

Reasoning, tool calls, tool outputs, file URLs, synthetic text, ignored text,
and child/subagent sessions are excluded.

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin -g @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0
```

Completely quit and restart OpenCode after installation. The first completed
turn is archived locally under `~/opencode-conversations` with no additional
setup.

See the [User Guide](./USER_GUIDE.md) for Second Brain connection, sharing one
remote repository with Claude Code, management commands, privacy details,
upgrades, troubleshooting, and removal.

## Install From Source

Build the package:

```bash
cd toolkits/opencode-conversation-archiver
npm install
npm run build
```

Register the built server entry in `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    "./toolkits/opencode-conversation-archiver/dist/server.js"
  ]
}
```

The path is relative to the config file. Quit and restart OpenCode after adding
or updating a plugin because configuration is loaded only at startup. To get
the immediate `/new` title reset when installing from source, also register
`./toolkits/opencode-conversation-archiver/dist/tui.js` in the `plugin` array of
`tui.json`. The `opencode plugin` installer registers both npm entry points
automatically.

For package distribution, the package exposes OpenCode's native `./server`
and `./tui` entries. `engines.opencode` stays `>=1.17.18 <2`: only the 1.x
loader checks it (against the upstream base version), and the 2.x loader
ignores `engines`, so the range keeps excluding pre-1.17.18 hosts without
blocking 2.x.

## OpenCode/GenCode 2.x

The existing configuration line works unchanged on 2.x, because 2.x
normalizes the 1.x `plugin` array into `plugins`:

```json
{ "plugin": [["@genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@latest", { "mode": "auto" }]] }
```

Each entry module has one default export that satisfies both loaders: 1.x
reads `{ id, server }` / `{ id, tui }` and ignores `setup`; 2.x requires
`{ id, setup }` (`Plugin.define` shape, resolved through the same `./server`
and `./tui` exports) and ignores `server`/`tui`. The modules import nothing at
runtime from either plugin SDK, so both `@opencode-ai/plugin` (1.x) and
`@opencode/plugin` (2.x) are optional type-only peers.

What differs on 2.x:

| | 1.x | 2.x |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn-end trigger | `session.status` idle event hook | `session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted}` via `ctx.event.subscribe` |
| Transcript source | `client.session.messages` (message + parts) | `ctx.session.get` + `ctx.session.context` (V2 message union), mapped to the same blocks |
| Tools | `tool` hook | `ctx.tool.transform` direct tools (`codemode: false`), same four names; writes use `ctx.permission.assert` |
| Turn-complete notification | written by the server process | the server is a shared background service with no terminal, so it emits a plugin RPC event and the TUI that drove the turn writes the notification |
| tmux coordinates in the archive | read from the server's environment | the TUI attaches its tmux session to each conversation it creates/runs over plugin RPC |
| `/new` reset | `session.new` command layer | `session.new` and `session.clear` command layer (`keymap.layer`, priority 100, returns `false` so the native command still runs) |
| TUI part registration | `tui.json` | automatic (2.x lists the package's `./tui` entry for the TUI) |

2.x exposes the active context window (everything from the latest compaction)
to plugins rather than the full transcript. Archive state only grows, so turns
archived before a compaction are kept; `backfill` of a session first seen after
a compaction archives from that compaction on.

## Default Behavior

- Archive repo: `~/opencode-conversations`
- Runtime state: `~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/`
- Mode: `auto`
- Trigger: canonical `session.status` event with `status.type === "idle"` on
  1.x; the end of each execution (`session.execution.*`) on 2.x
- Auto mode: write, commit, and launch a detached push after every changed turn
- Manual mode: write locally without commit or push
- No remote: commits remain local and push failure never interrupts OpenCode

## Terminal Notifications

The plugin emits OSC 9999 `genterm-notify` sequences (base64 JSON) to the
controlling terminal, wrapped in tmux passthrough under tmux. Each payload
carries the pane's tmux coordinates
(`tmux.{socket,session,windowId,windowIndex,windowName}`) so GenTerminal can
join `tmux.session` against its managed session record. Since 0.3.2 the TUI
plugin owns title-changing notifications: it reports each distinct
non-placeholder `session.updated` title and observes the native `session.new`
command to immediately report the directory basename (`body: "New
conversation"`), mirroring the cc plugin's `/clear` reset, while returning
control to OpenCode's native handler. The server still reports each archived
turn for inbox, activity, and unread tracking, but uses a dedicated
`<session-id>:idle` source ID and the non-renaming `OpenCode` placeholder so a
delayed old archive cannot restore an old title after `/new`. The command keeps
OpenCode's native command-palette and `/new`/`/clear` slash metadata.
`OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_NO_NOTIFY=1`
disables all notifications; `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_NOTIFY_TTY=<file>` redirects the
raw sequences to a file (the seam the tests use).

The server event hook owns a per-session archive queue because OpenCode
intentionally does not await plugin event callbacks. The TUI owns one ordered
notification queue so `/new` and subsequent model titles cannot reorder.
Both entry points drain their pending work during a clean shutdown. Git and
tmux commands use asynchronous child processes so archive work does not block
OpenCode's event loop.

## Management Tools

The plugin exposes these native tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `conversation_archive_status` | Mode, repo, redacted remote, commits, pending changes |
| `conversation_archive_doctor` | Read-only dependency, repo, remote-auth, and activity diagnosis |
| `conversation_archive_current` | Archive the current live session immediately |
| `conversation_archive_backfill` | Archive all top-level sessions visible in the current OpenCode project |

Users can ask OpenCode to invoke these tools naturally, for example: "diagnose
my conversation archive". The two write tools request explicit permission.
Credential-bearing and repository-management operations are CLI-only so their
arguments never enter an LLM-visible conversation or tool call.

OpenCode `1.17.18` does not expose a direct, no-LLM server slash-command handler.
Markdown commands always enter the prompt pipeline and `command.execute.before`
cannot short-circuit it. For deterministic automation, use the bundled CLI:

```bash
opencode-conversation-archiver status
opencode-conversation-archiver doctor
opencode-conversation-archiver manual
opencode-conversation-archiver auto
opencode-conversation-archiver upload
opencode-conversation-archiver repo ~/Documents/opencode-conversations
opencode-conversation-archiver connect '<sb-connect-link>'
```

`backfill` and `current` remain live tools because they require the injected
OpenCode SDK and current session identity.

## Second Brain

The CLI `connect` supports:

1. A one-time `.../sb-connect/<code>` URL.
2. No arguments, using `GSK_API_KEY` or the credential created by `gsk login`.
3. An explicit HTTP(S) git remote and token.

The git credential is stored at
`~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/git-credentials` with mode `0600`,
outside the archive repository. The remote URL shown by status, doctor, and logs
is credential-redacted. Connected archives are confined to the `opencode/`
subdirectory by default with sparse checkout.

## Configuration

Runtime configuration:

```json
{
  "mode": "auto",
  "repo": "/home/you/opencode-conversations",
  "subdir": "opencode"
}
```

Environment overrides:

- `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_MODE`
- `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_REPO`
- `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_NO_NOTIFY`

For isolated tests or embedded installations, pass `appDir` as plugin options:

```json
{
  "plugin": [
    [
      "@genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver",
      { "appDir": "/custom/runtime-state" }
    ]
  ]
}
```

## Preservation Guarantees

- Message and compaction part IDs make overlapping/repeated idle events idempotent.
- Cumulative text for an existing message ID can grow without duplicating a turn.
- Session state is append-only and outside the git repo.
- Title changes rename the archive while preserving git history where possible.
- A collision index prevents one session from overwriting another.
- A never-shrink guard diverts to a suffixed file if disk content is richer than
  local state, preserving both copies instead of dropping turns.
- Archive and push operations use cross-process lock directories.
- Remote pushes serialize, pull with rebase, and abort a failed in-progress rebase.

## Development

```bash
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm pack --dry-run
```

### Local End-to-End Verification

Version `0.4.0` was verified in Docker (non-root, isolated `HOME`) against
both GenCode `2.2.0-gencode.1-alpha.15` and `1.19.3-gencode.3`, each installing
the packed tarball from a local registry through the exact
`["@genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@latest", {"mode":"auto"}]` config
line with a scripted OpenAI-compatible model: `gencode run` turns were archived
and pushed to a local bare remote, all four tools answered through real tool
calls, and a tmux-driven TUI session produced the title, turn-complete and
`/new` notifications and recorded the tmux session in the archive.

Earlier releases:

The release was verified against a real local OpenCode `1.17.18` process, not
only mocked SDK tests. An isolated `opencode run` session using Claude Haiku
completed with `ARCHIVER_E2E_OK`; the plugin then created a titled Markdown
archive containing one user and one assistant turn and committed it to the
isolated archive git repository. The temporary plugin config and archive paths
were supplied through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `appDir`, and
`OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_REPO`, so the normal OpenCode configuration and archive were
not modified.

# OpenCode Conversation Archiver User Guide

OpenCode Conversation Archiver saves each top-level OpenCode chat as readable
Markdown and can synchronize it to a git repository. It archives completed
turns automatically without changing the conversation or blocking OpenCode.

## Requirements

- OpenCode/GenCode `1.17.18` or newer (1.x), or OpenCode/GenCode 2.x
  (archiver `0.4.0` or newer)
- Git on `PATH`
- Node.js 20 or newer for the management CLI

## Install

Install globally so the plugin is available in every OpenCode project:

```bash
opencode plugin -g @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0
```

To enable it only in the current project, omit `-g`:

```bash
opencode plugin @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0
```

OpenCode writes the package's server entry to the selected `opencode.json` and
its TUI entry to the matching `tui.json` (1.x). On 2.x one `plugin` (or
`plugins`) entry in `opencode.json` is enough: the TUI part loads
automatically. An existing 1.x configuration keeps working after upgrading
OpenCode/GenCode to 2.x; just make sure it resolves to archiver `0.4.0` or
newer (`@latest` does). On the next startup it installs and
caches the npm package automatically. Completely quit and restart OpenCode
after installing or upgrading the plugin.

To track the latest release rather than pinning a version:

```bash
opencode plugin -g @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver
```

## First Conversation

No setup is required for local archiving. After the next completed OpenCode
turn, the plugin creates:

```text
~/opencode-conversations/
└── YYYY-MM/
    └── YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-conversation-title.md
```

The directory is initialized as a git repository. With no remote configured,
archives are committed locally and push failures never interrupt OpenCode.

Check the setup from a terminal:

```bash
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 status
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 doctor
```

If the package is installed globally with npm, the shorter executable also
works:

```bash
opencode-conversation-archiver status
```

## Connect Second Brain

Use one of these methods from a terminal. Connection credentials are never
accepted through an LLM-visible OpenCode tool.

### One-Time Link

Copy the Second Brain connection link and run:

```bash
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 connect '<sb-connect-link>'
```

### Existing Genspark CLI Login

If `gsk login` has already created a local credential, run:

```bash
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 connect
```

The command can also use `GSK_API_KEY` from the environment.

### Explicit Git Remote

For another HTTP(S) git server:

```bash
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 \
  connect 'https://git.example.com/archive.git' '<token>' 'opencode'
```

`connect` succeeds only after the initial remote synchronization succeeds. A
partially configured connection with a failed first push exits nonzero so
scripts can detect and retry it.

## Share One Repository With Claude Code

Claude Code and OpenCode can synchronize to the same remote repository without
sharing a local working tree:

```text
Remote conversation repository
├── YYYY-MM/             Claude Code archives
└── opencode/
    └── YYYY-MM/         OpenCode archives
```

Recommended local layout:

```text
~/claude-conversations/     Claude Code clone and locks
~/opencode-conversations/   OpenCode clone and locks
```

Connect OpenCode to the same remote/token used by Claude Code, with `opencode`
as the subdirectory. The default Second Brain connection already uses this
layout.

Do not point both plugins at the same local clone. Each plugin performs its own
commit, rebase, push, state tracking, and locking. Separate clones prevent one
plugin from staging the other plugin's in-progress files while still producing
one combined remote history.

## Daily Use

Automatic mode is enabled by default. Each changed completed turn is written,
committed, and pushed in the background when a remote exists.

```bash
# Show mode, repository, redacted remote, recent commits, and pending changes
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 status

# Run read-only dependency, repository, and remote checks
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 doctor

# Keep writing Markdown locally without commit or push
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 manual

# Restore automatic commit and push
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 auto

# Commit and push pending archives immediately
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 upload

# Send future local archives to another dedicated clone
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 \
  repo ~/Documents/opencode-conversations
```

The `repo` command repoints future archives. It does not move or delete the old
repository.

## OpenCode Tools

The plugin gives OpenCode four tools:

| Tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `conversation_archive_status` | Read-only archive status |
| `conversation_archive_doctor` | Read-only diagnostics |
| `conversation_archive_current` | Archive the current top-level project session after permission approval |
| `conversation_archive_backfill` | Archive existing top-level sessions in the current project after permission approval |

Examples to type in OpenCode:

```text
Check my conversation archive status.
Diagnose my conversation archive.
Archive this conversation now.
Backfill this project's existing conversations.
```

Repository paths, modes, uploads, connection links, and tokens are CLI-only so
those values do not enter the model conversation.

## What Is Saved

Saved:

- User-visible user text
- User-visible assistant text
- Context compaction boundaries
- Session ID, start time, title, machine name, and turn count

Not saved:

- Reasoning parts
- Tool calls and tool outputs
- Uploaded file URLs
- Synthetic or ignored text parts
- Child/subagent sessions
- Git credentials

Credentials are stored outside the archive repository at:

```text
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/git-credentials
```

The file is created with mode `0600`. Status, doctor, and logs redact
credentials embedded in HTTP(S) URLs.

## Configuration And Files

Runtime configuration:

```text
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/config.json
```

Runtime state and logs:

```text
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/state/
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/archive.log
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/push.log
```

Environment overrides:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_MODE` | `auto` or `manual` |
| `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_REPO` | Override the local archive clone |
| `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_NO_NOTIFY` | Disable terminal completion and title notifications when set |

## Upgrade

Install a newer version with `--force`, then restart OpenCode:

```bash
opencode plugin -g -f @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0
```

Your Markdown repository and runtime state are outside OpenCode's plugin cache
and remain in place across upgrades.

## Troubleshooting

### No Markdown Appears

1. Completely restart OpenCode after installation.
2. Finish a top-level conversation turn; child/subagent sessions are excluded.
3. Run `doctor` and confirm Git is available.
4. Check the configured repository shown by `status`.

### Local Commit Exists But Remote Is Behind

Run:

```bash
npx -y @genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver@0.4.0 upload
```

Then run `doctor`. It tests remote authentication without printing the token.
The plugin serializes pushes and performs `pull --rebase` before pushing, so a
Claude Code commit arriving first is integrated into the same remote history.

### Connect Link Does Not Work

One-time links can expire or be consumed once. Generate a new link and run the
CLI command again. Do not paste the link into an OpenCode chat.

### OpenCode Loads The Plugin Twice

Check both global and project `opencode.json` and `tui.json`. Keep one npm entry
in each matching scope unless you intentionally need different project-specific
options. A local plugin file and an npm plugin are separate and can both load.

## Remove

Remove `@genspark/opencode-conversation-archiver` from the `plugin` arrays in
the project or global `opencode.json` and `tui.json`, then restart OpenCode.

Uninstalling does not delete either of these locations:

```text
~/opencode-conversations/
~/.config/opencode/conversation-archiver/
```

Delete or retain them according to your own backup policy.
